analysis.title: The Cheapest Crash Hedge On Wall Street Right Now Is...
key_insights: BofA argues credit is signaling rising macro stress while equities hold near highs. Credit spreads, especially high yield, widened materially over the past month. Rates and equity vol also rose. FX and commodity vol were the only segments to decline.

BofA's Global Financial Stress Indicator (GFSI) rose back above its long-run median to +0.09, the 57th percentile since 2000. Equities drove most of the move. HY and IG CDS posted the biggest stress increases of any cross-asset vol or spread. Rates vol remains the most stressed segment.
AI credit spreads and hyperscaler spreads are at the widest levels of the year. Oracle CDS has blown out. The last time spreads were nearly this high, the underlying equities were 15% lower.

BofA's cross-asset hedging screen divides the average of the ten worst 3-month drops since 2006 by the cost of a 3-month 25-delta put in implied vol terms. A higher ratio means more protection per unit of premium.

FX puts screen as the cheapest crash hedges across 31 assets. CADUSD puts rank first, followed by CDX IG, AUDUSD, GBPUSD and EURUSD. The bottom of the list is the Kospi, Nikkei, Bovespa, crude oil and the Nasdaq.
Equity hedges appear expensive regardless of the historical sample. China is the relative bright spot, where HSI and HSCEI puts offer better value than most other equity hedges.

BofA's screen differs from Goldman's vol desk view that SPX downside convexity is 'very offered' (Oct 12). Index puts can be cheap versus VIX calls and still be expensive versus historical equity crash payoffs.

Re-running the screen with data since 2021 only (excluding the GFC and COVID) sharply reduces the appeal of most credit hedges. The five biggest losers are CDX IG, CADUSD, HYG, iTraxx Main and CDX HY. CDX IG payers screen expensive on the past five years.
CADUSD remains ranked first on the post-2021 sample, with its ratio falling from about 3.7 to 1.7. Aluminium puts and gold calls also screen attractively post-2021 as cost-efficient protection.

Credit hedges can be cheap in vol terms and still have paid off poorly since 2021 because credit has not crashed in that period. This contrasts with Goldman credit strategists' Macro Credit Hedge Menu (Oct 7).

Bonus trade: buy an SX7E Jun27 260 put (~30-delta, ref 283.7) for 5.7%, funded by selling 8.8x notional of 5Y Senior Financials CDS protection at 72bp. Example sizing is EUR100mn of CDS against EUR11.4mn of SX7E.
European bank Senior Financials CDS have widened toward the top of their three-year range. The SX7E index is only about 12% off its all-time high after a roughly 200% rally over three years.

The author's view is that credit hedges look cheap only if the past five years of credit calm are the anomaly. Credit spreads have been held tight by yield-hungry buyers while AI capex borrowing pushes hyperscaler CDS to records. The author plans to revisit after megacap earnings.

vol_and_positioning: Credit spreads, especially high yield, widened materially over the past month. Rates and equity vol rose. FX and commodity vol were the only segments to decline.
Rates vol remains the most stressed segment in BofA's GFSI.

FX puts are the cheapest tail hedges in BofA's 31-asset screen, led by CADUSD, with CDX IG, AUDUSD, GBPUSD and EURUSD next. Nasdaq, crude, Bovespa, Nikkei and Kospi puts are the most expensive relative to historical crash size.
HSI and HSCEI puts offer better value than most other equity hedges. Equity hedges in general look expensive across historical samples.
On a post-2021 sample, CADUSD still ranks first with its ratio falling from about 3.7 to 1.7. Aluminium puts and gold calls also screen well, while CDX IG, HYG, iTraxx Main and CDX HY drop sharply.

Hedge idea: buy SX7E Jun27 260 put (~30-delta, ref 283.7) for 5.7%, funded by selling 8.8x notional of 5Y Senior Financials CDS protection at 72bp. If spreads return to YTD wides and the SX7E falls to its YTD low, the payoff is roughly 25x the average outcome in the unchanged scenarios.

tension_points.bull_case: CDX IG and other credit hedges screen among the cheapest on the full history because spreads blew out in the GFC and COVID, and credit is already flashing stress while equities hold near highs.
tension_points.bear_case: Excluding the GFC and COVID, credit hedges lose much of their appeal and CDX IG payers screen outright expensive over the past five years. Credit protection only looks like a bargain if spreads blow out like in 2008.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Credit keeps widening while bank stocks refuse to fall, which breaks the SX7E put and Senior Financials CDS funding trade.
